bug_semantics: An authenticated user could submit an arbitrary tag icon through POST /tags/create. The backend stored data.icon without validation, and the reusable Vue tag component later passed tag.icon to mapIcon(), which interpolated the value into an HTML string and rendered that string through v-html. A value that closed the class attribute and supplied attacker-controlled markup therefore became stored XSS when the tag was rendered, including in the administrative tag-triage interface.
flaw_origin: Commit 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb introduced the complete exploitable mechanism in one ordinary, single-parent change: website/web/static/js/tags/utils/galaxie.js created mapIcon() with an unconstrained template-literal HTML return; website/web/static/js/tags/singleTagDisplay.js rendered that return with v-html; website/web/tags/tags.py passed request JSON's icon directly into persistent tag creation; and website/web/templates/admin/admin_tags.html wired SingleTagDisplay into the admin list. These vulnerable frontend files did not exist in the direct parent.
ai_marker: absent: the exact commit object for 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb names author ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com> and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>; its message is only 'chg: [tag] new way to manage tag' and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory metadata at https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3VX2-8R8R-PF7R and https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3vx2-8r8r-pf7r describes the stored-XSS path: user-supplied tag.icon was interpolated by mapIcon() into and rendered via Vue v-html. It references the repository fix https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/cc13416d606d91d543ce1f1e41387750f8450153.

The validated clone is full history (git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository returned false). git log --all --reverse -S for the exact vulnerable mapIcon return over website/web/static/js/tags/utils/galaxie.js found 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb as the addition and cc13416d606d91d543ce1f1e41387750f8450153 as its removal. A broader all-history -G search for mapIcon, v-html icon use, or icon interpolation likewise began at 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb.

At 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb, website/web/static/js/tags/utils/galaxie.js:17-20 defines mapIcon(), assigns icon directly to name (apart from a default), and returns an HTML template string. website/web/static/js/tags/singleTagDisplay.js:65-67 and :83-87 send mapIcon(tag.icon) to v-html. website/web/tags/tags.py:235-265 accepts authenticated POST /tags/create JSON and passes data.get("icon") to TagsModel.create_tag without validation. website/web/templates/admin/admin_tags.html:97,172-180,206,298,317 uses SingleTagDisplay as tag-chip in the administrative tag interface.

Direct-parent verification: git ls-tree -r --name-only b608b50a41c4eb2e73738f6a29a297d67c0d2ebf -- website/web/static/js/tags returned no paths. git grep in that exact parent tree for mapIcon, v-html applied to an icon, and the vulnerable template literal returned no match anywhere under website. The BIC diff creates galaxie.js and singleTagDisplay.js from /dev/null, so the vulnerable helper and sinks are absent in the immediate parent, not merely modified or moved.

78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb has exactly one parent, b608b50a41c4eb2e73738f6a29a297d67c0d2ebf, and directly creates the vulnerable source files. No merge, revert, move, backport, release aggregate, or reconstructable squash member intervenes, so decomposition is not applicable.

Version boundary: git tag --contains 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb returned v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5; it did not return v1.2. The first affected release page https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/releases/tag/v1.3 resolves to commit ecd04d494b0fda2ab39fb56472785388c2d5872e and documents the expanded tag system. Thus the BIC lands after v1.2 and before v1.3.

Fixed boundary: git tag --contains cc13416d606d91d543ce1f1e41387750f8450153 returned only v1.5. The first-party v1.5 release at https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/releases/tag/v1.5 resolves to fe093f9a1f9727068bc7e82ba47630907d859edb, states that all users of 1.4 and earlier should upgrade, and explicitly lists CVE-2026-73159 / GCVE-1-2026-20164 as stored XSS via the tag icon field affecting 1.3-1.4. This corroborates v1.3-v1.4 vulnerable and v1.5 fixed.

The direct fix cc13416d606d91d543ce1f1e41387750f8450153 removes v-html icon rendering in website/web/static/js/tags/multiTagFilter.js and website/web/static/js/tags/singleTagDisplay.js, changes website/web/static/js/tags/utils/galaxie.js mapIcon() to return only a constrained CSS class string, and adds server-side FontAwesome-catalogue/slug validation on create and edit in website/web/tags/tags.py. It is the advisory-linked source fix rather than a release wrapper or backport.

BIC-only AI inspection used git cat-file commit 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb. The raw commit object contains tree 589f1753f566e5059ccf53b8678b5f2b094adc74, the direct parent, human author/committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>, and the one-line subject, with no AI authorship identity or trailer. No later commit, advisory prose, PR metadata, or fix attribution was used to classify the BIC.
reasoning: The vulnerability-first trace starts with the advisory's specific taint flow and reproduces it in history: attacker-controlled request JSON enters the icon field, is stored without a constraint, is returned as tag.icon, is concatenated into markup by mapIcon(), and reaches Vue's HTML-parsing v-html sink. The smallest commit that first makes that flow possible is 78c528c22a83fbfa01a87a708b78abea5199aebb, because it simultaneously creates the vulnerable helper and SingleTagDisplay sinks and retains the unvalidated storage path; exact-string and regex history searches find no earlier source origin. Its immediate parent b608b50a41c4eb2e73738f6a29a297d67c0d2ebf has neither the frontend path nor any matching mechanism, proving parent absence. Tag containment and the maintainer's v1.5 security table place exposure in v1.3-v1.4 and remediation in v1.5. Advisory-linked commit cc13416d606d91d543ce1f1e41387750f8450153 directly breaks the flow at all relevant layers. Finally, the raw BIC commit object has human author and committer identities and no AI marker, so under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
